transcript.text: Hey, Alex. I may have to let go of 200
employees overnight. I run a company
that sells furniture. For years, US
buyers have been one of our biggest
markets, but with all this talk of a
huge tariff on furniture imports, this
could be the first time trade policy is
threatening my entire business. What do
I even do here?
>> So, number one is if I can, I'm not
going to think about it. If you do think
it's going to be a material threat to
the business, then what you need to do
is have a plan. If this happens, what
will I do? What is it going to change?
And then you come up with the plan. And
then once you have the plan written out,
you put it away, and then you just keep
doing business. One of the hardest parts
of entrepreneurship is that you have
often times lose-lose decisions.
Because, and I think Ben Horowitz said
this, the win-lose decisions are very
easy to make. You don't even think about
them because they're just the obvious
choice. The hard choice is where you
have to choose between two terrible
things, and you have to pick the lesser
of two evils. I am tortured by this
decision. It has kept me up for nights,
and I've been hoping and praying that
this tariff didn't happen because I knew
that if it did, I would have to pick
between having some people uh lose their
jobs and having everyone lose their
jobs. My biggest thing with this stuff
is when I have those hard decisions or
hard announcements, state the facts and
tell the truth.
